cards.title: Decide how Google sign-in reaches a hosted address: Flowform widened, or Foundation's own Google client
cards.body: The blocker for a hosted Foundation (Josh, 2026-11-20: company-wide chat comes from hosting Foundation's own server, not Mattermost, and not Tailscale as the way in: ChatForm is already the chat server, and keeping chat beside the boards is what lets agents read and answer in it.) Sign-in goes through Flowform, whose callback rule takes only a loopback address (http, 127.0.0.1 or localhost, a port), so a server at an https address can't finish a sign-in: `loopbackOrigin()` in apps/server/src/flowform.ts refuses one. Two ways, a person's choice: (a) Flowform widens `native_loopback_callback` to accept the hosted address (a change on Flowform's side; Foundation keeps one sign-in for the company), or (b) Foundation gets its own Google OAuth client (`GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` / `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`, an internal consent screen on the Form Industries Google Workspace). SPEC §6 #2. *hosted-signin* builds whichever is chosen. 2026-11-20: (b) is built and checked with a stand-in Google, because it needs nothing from Flowform. What is left is a person's: create the OAuth client (docs/hosting.md) and put its ID and secret on the hosted machine. Say so if (a) is wanted instead.

cards.title: Choose where the hosted Foundation runs and its address
cards.body: A person's choice and accounts (Josh, 2026-11-20: company-wide chat comes from hosting Foundation's own server, not Mattermost, and not Tailscale as the way in: ChatForm is already the chat server, and keeping chat beside the boards is what lets agents read and answer in it.) Where: a small cloud VM (simplest, always on) or an always-on computer in the office. Its name: for example foundation.formindustries.com, with DNS pointed at it. Who pays, and who holds the machine's keys. Whether it's open to the internet (Google sign-in is the fence) or only reachable on the company's private network (Tailscale in front). *hosted-deploy* makes it runnable; this card says where. 2026-11-20: either choice now runs from deploy/compose.yml (docs/hosting.md): a VM with ports 80/443 uses Caddy; a computer with no open ports uses the tunnel profile. Also set FOUNDATION_ALLOWLIST to the domains people really sign in with (the default says formindustries.com; HyperForm's accounts are formindustries.co and normallab.co). 2026-11-20, Josh: a cloud VM. deploy/setup-vm.sh readies an Ubuntu 24.04 VM (Docker, firewall, the repo, deploy/.env); not yet run on a real one. Still a person's: which provider and account, the VM itself, the name and its DNS record.

cards.title: Until hosting: two computers share one Foundation through an SSH tunnel over Tailscale
cards.body: A stopgap for Josh's home and work computers, not the company's way in (Josh, 2026-11-20: company-wide chat comes from hosting Foundation's own server, not Mattermost, and not Tailscale as the way in: ChatForm is already the chat server, and keeping chat beside the boards is what lets agents read and answer in it.) The home computer runs the app's built-in server (it stays up while the app is open); the work computer forwards its own localhost:4410 to it, so the work app finds a server on :4410, uses it, and the Flowform sign-in returns through the tunnel. Nothing in Foundation changes and nothing is on the open internet. Home (admin PowerShell): `winget install --id Tailscale.Tailscale`, `Add-WindowsCapability -Online -Name OpenSSH.Server~~~~0.0.1.0`, `Start-Service sshd; Set-Service sshd -StartupType Automatic`; keep Foundation open and the PC awake. Work: Tailscale on the same account, quit Foundation, then `ssh -N -L 4410:127.0.0.1:4410 <you>@<home-pc>` and open Foundation. Not run yet. Work IT may not allow Tailscale; huddles connect directly and may fail on a strict network.

(2) Rune's accessibility mirror left each link's <a> taking the pointer above the canvas, so the browser opened the address itself, round openExternal, and Rune heard nothing; rune.css keeps the pointer off the mirror. All 11 checks pass. Still unexplained: 'a section's tools, rename, drag…' failed twice at the drag-swap and then passed eight times on the same code; if it comes back, look for a cancelled pointer (the drop arrives as 'cancel'). A person checks: a link in a note under Rune in the desktop app.
